outline.rationale: The user wants a practical, working grasp of writing a PRD for a solo side project, used as a thinking tool rather than a stakeholder-alignment artifact. I included the core building blocks confirmed as priorities: problem framing, users, scope, requirements, and success criteria. I added a short "what is a PRD for" node because the user wants a working understanding (not assumed prior knowledge), and an assumptions/risks node since solo founders benefit greatly from surfacing unknowns. The final node addresses how to actually assemble and right-size the doc, matching their goal of "actually producing one." I deliberately excluded process-heavy nodes (approval workflows, stakeholder sign-off, cross-team coordination, roadmapping/release planning) per the deprioritization signal. Nodes are MECE-ish: problem, users, scope, requirements, and metrics each cover distinct content with low overlap, ordered by natural dependency.
